keeps.name: Shambo (Beaver Creek Park)
keeps.waterfront_evidence: NAIP summer imagery (USGS) at 48.2813,-109.6619: drive-in sites tucked into the wooded belt along Beaver Creek, trailers ~25-50 m from the channel behind trees and brush (Hagener end at 48.2697,-109.6596 ~50 m); the one open pad (48.2811,-109.6607) sits ~25 m off the channel with brush between; canopy hides the rest and the bcpark.org park map is an overview with no per-site layout -> default down. Stored pin 48.3079,-109.6594 was the RV dump lot, not a campground.
keeps.inclusion_evidence: bcpark.org (Hill County) camping page, read 2026-10-24: 'over 100' non-reservable, first-come rustic sites with a park permit, 'the majority of all available camping is on the south end of the Park'; the park map PDF marks campground symbols and the non-group areas Shambo, Doney and Hagener on Beaver Creek east of MT-234 between Shambo Loop and Pine Coulee. NAIP summer imagery shows drive-in dirt/gravel spurs and loops here with travel trailers ~9-10 m (about 30 ft) long parked at sites (48.2843,-109.6635; 48.2810,-109.6620; 48.2697,-109.6596). The county posts no length limit (silent -> keep).
keeps.note: Hill County's Beaver Creek Park in the Bears Paw Mountains south of Havre: the first-come sites in the trees along Beaver Creek east of MT-234, from Shambo Loop south past Taylor Road to Pine Coulee, about 1.5 km south of the park office at Camp Kiwanis. The park map names Shambo, Doney and Hagener here; Dean Hanson, Rotary (on Rotary Pond), J.C. Park and H.F.D. among them are reservable group sites. Cattle graze the park after Labor Day. --Claude

facilities.note: No dump or water in this part of the park: the park's RV dump is about 3 km north near mile marker 18 and the potable water fill stations are in front of the park office at Camp Kiwanis, about 1.5 km north. Picnic table, fire pit or ring and trash cans at sites; an outhouse within walking distance of most.

adds.name: Springs Campground (Beaver Creek Park)
adds.note: Hill County's Beaver Creek Park near its south end, about 21 miles south of Havre on MT-234: the first-come sites in the trees along Beaver Creek from below Alkali Springs Road south past Brough Coulee to Black Coulee. The park map names Springs Campground and Hidden Hollows here; Lions A and B, R.R.P.A. and H.P.P.A. among them are reservable group sites. The Bear Paw Nature Trail runs along the canyon's west side above them. Cattle graze the park after Labor Day. --Claude
adds.inclusion_evidence: bcpark.org (Hill County) camping page, read 2026-10-24: 'over 100' non-reservable, first-come rustic sites with a park permit, most on the south end of the park; the park map PDF marks campground symbols for Hidden Hollows, Springs Campground and the unnamed sites off Alkali Springs and Black Coulee roads (group sites marked separately in pink). NAIP summer imagery shows dirt spurs off MT-234 into the creek-bottom timber with travel trailers ~10-12 m long parked at sites (48.2414,-109.6572; 48.2475,-109.6572; 48.2315,-109.6575). The county posts no length limit (silent -> keep).
adds.waterfront_evidence: NAIP summer imagery at 48.2414,-109.6572 and 48.2315,-109.6575: sites under dense conifer/aspen canopy ~30-40 m west of Beaver Creek, channel mostly hidden; no per-site map (bcpark.org park map is an overview) -> canopy-blind, default down.

facilities.note: No dump or water at this end of the park: the RV dump is near mile marker 18, about 7.5 km north, and the potable water fill stations are at the park office (Camp Kiwanis), about 6 km north. Picnic table, fire pit or ring and trash cans at sites; an outhouse within walking distance of most.

adds.name: Beaver Creek Reservoir (Beaver Creek Park)
adds.note: Hill County's Beaver Creek Park at its north entrance, about 10 miles south of Havre on MT-234: first-come sites on open grass loops around Beaver Creek Reservoir (First Lake), on the east-shore peninsulas and along the west shore past the dam. No-wake lake, boats limited to 10 hp; the fishing pier belongs to the Community Effort group site, and the park information kiosk and self-pay box are at the lake. Cattle graze the park after Labor Day. --Claude
adds.inclusion_evidence: bcpark.org (Hill County) non-reservable campsites section, read 2026-10-24: 'Beaver Creek Park offers many non-reservable campsites ... The park map indicates a few of these campsite locations including some at Beaver Creek Lake. Park permits are required'; the park map PDF puts campground symbols on the reservoir's east and west shores (Community Effort, marked pink, is the group site). NAIP imagery shows drive-in two-track loops on open grass (48.4136,-109.7232; 48.4115,-109.7228; 48.4128,-109.7310) with a ~8-10 m trailer parked on the east loop. The county posts no length limit (silent -> keep).
adds.waterfront_evidence: NAIP imagery (USGS) at 48.4135,-109.7233: the east-shore peninsula's drive-in two-track loop runs over open, unused grass 15-20 m from the beach edge, with the parked trailer ~35 m back, nothing but grass and beach between (open apron within the bound); a second loop at 48.4115,-109.7228 is the same; the west-shore loop at 48.4128,-109.7310 also sits on open ground at the shore. Sites at 941 m match the open-water DEM (941 m), and the dam is at the reservoir's north-west corner (crest ~48.418,-109.733), so these sit on the pool rather than below the dam. Agrees with the wf-mt-5 lead (13-17 m).

facilities.note: No dump or water at the reservoir: the park's RV dump is near mile marker 18, about 13 km south, and the potable water fill stations are in front of the park office at Camp Kiwanis. Picnic table, fire pit or ring and trash cans at sites; outhouses at the lake.

excluded.name: Bearpaw Lake Fishing Access Site (Bear Paw Lake / Second Lake)
excluded.reason: Run by Montana FWP, not the county; the FWP fishing access page posts 'Trailer Length is 20ft' (and a 7-day stay limit) -> under EKKO's 23 ft, not added.

excluded.name: Reservable group campgrounds: Community Effort, Darel Marden Memorial, Elks, Eagles, Dean Hanson Memorial, Rotary, J.C. Park, H.F.D., Bear Paw Bowmen, Mardens, Havre Fire Dept, HPPA, JC's, Lions A, Lions B, Railroad Pagers, R.R.P.A.
excluded.reason: Group-only: bcpark.org says these 'can be reserved for larger group activities' by the whole weekend and are pink with an asterisk on the park map; individual campers use the non-reservable areas above.

excluded.name: Camp Kiwanis and Chapel
excluded.reason: Lodge, 13 cabins and rec hall rented whole to groups ('sleeps up to 150'); cabin/group facility, not RV camping. It is the park office.

excluded.name: Boy Scout Camp
excluded.reason: Youth group camp (OSM camp_site, access=private, group_only=yes, 48.3121,-109.6579), not public camping.

excluded.name: Zartman Memorial and Woodring Memorial
excluded.reason: Marked as picnic grounds (P), not campgrounds, on the park map.

excluded.name: Scattered sites in the northern half (south of Crystal Springs/Eagle Rock roads, at Eagle Rock near Mountain View Road, near Reum Road)
excluded.reason: The county says only to 'look closely as you drive through the northern half of the Park for some sites there'; NAIP shows single roadside pull-offs/clearings several km apart (e.g. a gravel flat at 48.3598,-109.6705 under Eagle Rock, a turnout at 48.3825,-109.6790), with no loops and no rigs parked. Not campgrounds, and the imagery cannot show that any of them takes a 23-ft rig. Left out rather than given an entry each; the coordinator may revisit.
